# Category Act Title Section / Rule Statutory Clause Text
#1 Definitions Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 2(7) Under Section 2(7), a 'Consumer' is any person who buys goods or hires services for consideration, but excludes anyone who obtains goods for resale or commercial purposes.
#2 Definitions Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 2(10) Under Section 2(10), a 'Defect' means any fault, imperfection, or shortcoming in quality, quantity, potency, purity, or standard required by law or contract.
#3 Definitions Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 2(11) Under Section 2(11), a 'Deficiency' means any fault, imperfection, shortcoming, or inadequacy in the quality, nature, and manner of performance of a service.
#4 Definitions Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 2(47) Under Section 2(47), an 'Unfair Trade Practice' includes false representation of goods, misleading warranty claims, failure to issue bill/cash memo, and refusing to take back defective goods.
#5 Definitions Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 2(28) Under Section 2(28), misleading advertisements falsely describe products, give false guarantees, or deliberately conceal important information from consumers.
#6 Consumer Rights Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 2(9)(i) Consumers have the right to be protected against marketing of goods, products, and services that are hazardous to life and property.
#7 Consumer Rights Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 2(9)(ii) Consumers have the right to be informed about the quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard, and price of goods or services to prevent unfair practices.
#8 Consumer Rights Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 2(9)(iii) Consumers have the right to be assured access to a variety of goods and services at competitive prices wherever possible.
#9 Consumer Rights Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 2(9)(iv) Consumers have the right to be heard and assured that their interests will receive due consideration in appropriate consumer forums.
#10 Consumer Rights Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 2(9)(v) Consumers have the right to seek redressal against unfair trade practices or exploitation, and the right to consumer awareness and education.
#11 CCPA Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 10 Under Section 10, the Central Government establishes the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) to protect, promote, and enforce consumer rights as a class.
#12 CCPA Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 20 Under Section 20, the CCPA has the statutory power to order recall of dangerous goods, refund of prices paid, and discontinuation of unfair trade practices.
#13 CCPA Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 21 Under Section 21, the CCPA can impose penalties up to ₹10 Lakhs on manufacturers and endorsers for misleading ads, rising up to ₹50 Lakhs for subsequent violations.
#14 CCPA Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 21(2) The CCPA can prohibit a celebrity endorser of a misleading advertisement from making any endorsement for up to 1 year, and up to 3 years for subsequent violations.
#15 Redressal Commission Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 34 Under Section 34, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission entertains complaints where the value of goods or services paid does not exceed ₹50 Lakhs.
#16 Redressal Commission Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 47 Under Section 47, the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission entertains complaints where value exceeds ₹50 Lakhs but does not exceed ₹2 Crores.
#17 Redressal Commission Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 58 Under Section 58, the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) entertains complaints where the value exceeds ₹2 Crores.
#18 Redressal Commission Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 69 Under Section 69, a consumer complaint must be filed within 2 years from the date on which the cause of action arose.
#19 Redressal Commission Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 41 Under Section 41, any person aggrieved by an order of the District Commission may prefer an appeal to the State Commission within 45 days from the date of the order.
#20 Redressal Commission Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 35 & Rules Complaints filed in the District Commission with claims up to ₹5 Lakhs are completely exempt from paying any court or application fee.
#21 E-Commerce Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 Rule 4(4) Every e-commerce entity must appoint a nodal grievance officer and acknowledge consumer complaints within 48 hours.
#22 E-Commerce Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 Rule 4(5) E-commerce entities must resolve consumer grievances within 1 month (30 days) from the date of receipt of the complaint.
#23 E-Commerce Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 Rule 5(1) E-commerce platforms must clearly display the country of origin, expiry date, manufacturer details, and total price with breakup for all listed goods.
#24 E-Commerce Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 Rule 6 E-commerce sellers cannot impose cancellation charges on consumers unless similar charges are borne by the seller for unilateral cancellations.
#25 E-Commerce Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 Rule 6(2) E-commerce entities are prohibited from organizing fraudulent flash sales or back-to-back sales that limit consumer choice or artificially inflate prices.
#26 Product Liability Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 84 Under Section 84, a product manufacturer is liable in a product liability action if the product has a manufacturing defect, defective design, or lacks adequate warning instructions.
#27 Product Liability Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 85 Under Section 85, a product service provider is liable for harm caused if the service provided was deficient, negligent, or violated safety standards.
#28 Mediation Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 74 Under Section 74, the State Government establishes Consumer Mediation Cells attached to District and State Commissions to resolve disputes through voluntary mediation.
#29 Penalties Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 72 Under Section 72, failure to comply with an order of the District, State, or National Commission is punishable with imprisonment between 1 month to 3 years, or fine from ₹25,000 to ₹1 Lakh, or both.
#30 Penalties Consumer Protection Act, 2019 Section 35 Under Section 35, where the Commission finds a complaint to be frivolous or vexatious, it may dismiss the complaint and order the complainant to pay costs up to ₹50,000 to the opposite party.
